cards.text: Isaiah, God's prophet, is looking ahead to a day that's coming. He says that in that day, a song will be sung in the land of Judah. And the first thing the singers talk about is their strong city.

cards.question: In the song Judah will sing, salvation is what makes up the strong city's walls and ramparts.

cards.text: Next line: open the gates, somebody's coming in. And friend, it's not about who you know, because there's no VIP list at THIS door.

cards.question: The song calls out: Open the gates so a ___ nation may enter, one that remains faithful.

cards.text: Then the song makes a promise: God will keep the steadfast of mind in perfect peace. PERFECT peace, baker, and I spent years in a drawer next to dead batteries arguing all night about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: Why does God keep the steadfast of mind in perfect peace?

cards.text: So the song gives everybody one instruction. Trust in the LORD.

cards.question: The song says: Trust in the LORD ___, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.

cards.text: Then the song looks at the people who dwell on high, in the lofty city. God humbles them and brings that city all the way down into the dust.

cards.question: The lofty city is lying in the dust. Whose feet trample it down?

cards.text: Now the song says the path of the righteous is level, because God clears a straight path for the upright. Baker, my whole planet is ONE bakery big, and I still take wrong turns.

cards.question: As they walk in the path of God's judgments, the singers say they wait for the LORD.
The singers are waiting for the LORD. What do they say is the desire of their souls?

cards.text: Then the singer gets personal: "My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn." Night AND dawn, baker, before the snooze button even gets a vote.

cards.question: The singer says something happens when God's judgments come upon the earth. What is it?

answers.text: The people of the world learn righteousness
The mountains of the world melt like wax
The rivers of the world turn to blood

cards.question: The song says that when grace is shown to the wicked man, he learns righteousness too.

cards.text: He's right there in the land of righteousness, acting unjustly, and he fails to see the majesty of the LORD. That's a man standing in the middle of a bakery asking where the cookies are.

cards.question: Right after the wicked man, the song says God's hand is upraised, but they do not see it. What does the song say they will see?

cards.text: They'll see it and be put to shame. And the song says the fire set for God's enemies will consume them.
Then the singers say, "O LORD, You will establish peace for us." And they look back at everything they've ever gotten done.

cards.question: Looking back at all they've accomplished, who do the singers say actually did it?

answers.text: The LORD did it for them
Their kings did it for them
Their army did it for them

cards.question: Other lords besides God have ruled over the singers. Even so, they say they confess the LORD's name alone.

cards.text: Then the song says, "The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise." God has punished and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.

cards.question: Then the song turns to God's own nation, and the singers say twice that He has enlarged it. What does the song say He has extended?

answers.text: All the borders of the land
All the days of their kings

cards.text: Then the song remembers the hard times. When God disciplined them, they sought Him in their distress.

cards.question: In their distress, when God disciplined them, what did they pour out?

cards.text: Then the singers paint a picture of themselves. They say they were like a woman about to give birth, writhing and crying out in pain in the LORD's presence.

cards.question: The singers felt like a woman about to give birth. After all that pain, what did they give birth to?

cards.text: All that pain and it's WIND, with no salvation given to the earth and no life brought into the world. That's me in my worn-out days, pressing down HARD on the dough and lifting up a blur.

cards.question: Earlier the song said, "The dead will not live." Now it speaks about God's own people. Their dead will stay in the dust too.

cards.text: The song says, "Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!" Friend, I lay in the dust of a junk drawer for YEARS, and that line makes me hop my whole gold base around the bakery.

cards.question: God's people are told to awake and sing. What does the song say the earth will bring forth?
Then a call goes out to God's people to enter their rooms and shut their doors: Hide yourselves a little while until the ___ has passed.

cards.text: Why hide? Because the LORD is coming out of His dwelling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.

cards.question: When the LORD comes out of His dwelling, the earth will keep concealing her slain.

cards.text: Then in that day, the LORD takes His sharp, great and mighty sword. He brings judgment on Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, the coiling serpent.

cards.question: The LORD has His sword out against Leviathan. What does He do to the dragon of the sea?

cards.text: You can flee, you can coil, you can be a whole DRAGON of the sea. The LORD has a sharp, great and mighty sword, and that's the end of that.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 11 quotes "The dead will not live.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Isaiah is God's prophet, which is a fact from outside the passage, but it cites only Isaiah 26:1. It needs the reference where Isaiah is named, such as Isaiah 1:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke "it's not about who you know, because there's no VIP list at THIS door" points away from status-based answers. That rules out "mighty" and "wealthy" before card 4 asks the question. It also suggests there is no entry requirement, when 26:2 names one: righteous and faithful.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The song gives everybody one instruction" names who is being told to trust. Isaiah 26:4 does not say who the command is spoken to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "The people who dwell on high, in the lofty city" places those who dwell on high inside the lofty city. Isaiah 26:5 sets the two side by side and never states how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "The path of the righteous is level, because God clears a straight path" adds "because." Isaiah 26:7 joins the two lines with a semicolon and does not say one causes the other.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer "Nothing but wind" has an emphatic twist the other answers lack, so it stands out. "Nothing but" also goes further than the text, which says only "we gave birth to wind."

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question says verse 19 "speaks about God's own people." Isaiah 26:19 says only "Your dead," and it does not say who they are.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup "Earlier the song said... Now it speaks about..." frames verse 19 as a contrast with verse 14. That signals the statement with "too" is false, so the baker doesn't have to reason from the text.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The rest of Isaiah 26:19, "For your dew is like the dew of the morning," is never told or asked. The stop moves from the first half of the verse straight to "the earth will bring forth her dead," so the dew picture is lost.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "God's people are told to awake and sing" changes who is addressed. Isaiah 26:19 says "Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!"

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "A call goes out to God's people" makes God the speaker of "Go, my people." Isaiah 26:20 does not say who is speaking, and 26:21 refers to the LORD in the third person.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The last story card repeats the fleeing and coiling serpent and the "sharp, great and mighty sword" from card 17, and adds nothing new from 27:1. It is a recap and does not move the passage forward.
